name: YouTube Shorts
seo_title: YouTube Shorts and Kids: Parent's Guide (2026)
seo_description: Is YouTube Shorts safe for kids? How the endless Shorts feed works, the risks, and how to set a daily Shorts limit, or turn the feed off, for your child.
h1: YouTube Shorts: a guide for parents
lead: Shorts is YouTube's answer to TikTok: an endless feed of short videos, built into the YouTube app most children already use. It's also the one part of YouTube that parents can now switch off.
answer: Shorts carries the same risks as TikTok: an addictive feed and recommendations you don't choose. If your child has a supervised account or a supervised teen account, you can set a daily Shorts limit, including zero.

sections.heading: What are YouTube Shorts?
body: Shorts are vertical videos up to three minutes long. They play one after another in a feed: swipe up and the next one starts. Anyone with an account can make them, and they appear in the YouTube app, on the website and on smart TVs.
Children need to be 13 for their own YouTube account. Younger children can use YouTube through a parent-managed supervised account.

subsections.heading: The endless scroll
body: There's no natural stopping point, and each video is short enough that "just one more" turns into an hour. It's especially hard to put down at bedtime.

subsections.heading: Recommendations
body: The feed learns from what they watch and how long they linger, and can quickly fill up with extreme, frightening or body image content.

subsections.heading: Trends and challenges
body: Dangerous stunts, pranks and "challenges" spread fast in Shorts, and children may try to copy them.

subsections.heading: Comments and posting
body: If your child makes Shorts, strangers can comment on them, and videos of them can be shared well beyond their friends.

sections.heading: Set a Shorts limit
body: For a child's supervised account, go to families.youtube.com or the Family Link app. For a teen, in YouTube go to You, then Settings, then Family Centre, and invite them to supervision. Both of you have to agree, and either of you can end it.
list: Set a daily limit on the Shorts feed (zero turns it off)
Turn on Take a Break and bedtime reminders
Choose a content setting that fits their age
Block channels you don't want them to see
If they post, keep their videos private or unlisted

sections.heading: Age checks in the UK
body: YouTube uses age estimation in the UK. If it thinks a signed-in user is under 18, it blocks age-restricted videos and turns on break and bedtime reminders, even if the account says they're older.

sections.heading: Signs something's wrong
list: Getting very upset or angry when asked to stop
Scrolling late at night, or tiredness in the day
Copying stunts or challenges they've seen
Seeming low, anxious or unhappy with their body after watching

sections.heading: What parents can do
body: Sit with them for five minutes of their Shorts feed. It tells you more than any setting. Then agree on a limit together, rather than imposing one, and keep phones out of bedrooms at night.
list: "Show me the best Short you've seen this week."
"How do you feel after a long scroll?"
"Have you seen a challenge that looked dangerous?"

sections.heading: The UK under-16 plan
body: The government plans to stop social media companies providing their services to under-16s, and YouTube is one of the platforms named. It isn't law yet: the rules are due to go to Parliament in December 2026, with the ban starting from late spring 2027.

teachers: Shorts trends often show up in the playground within days. If a dangerous challenge is circulating, talk about it calmly without showing the video or naming it in a way that sends pupils to look it up.

faq.q: Can I turn off YouTube Shorts?
faq.a: Yes, for a supervised child or teen account. Set the daily Shorts limit to zero and the Shorts feed is switched off.
Up to three minutes each. They play one after another, so time adds up quickly.

faq.q: Is YouTube Shorts the same as TikTok?
faq.a: It works in much the same way, with an endless feed of short videos picked for each viewer. The difference is that it's built into YouTube.

faq.q: What age is YouTube Shorts for?
faq.a: Children need to be 13 for their own YouTube account. Younger children can watch through a supervised account set up by a parent.

help: Worried about something your child has seen? Childline is free and confidential on [0800 1111](tel:08001111), any time. You are not alone.
